Hi Jasmine,

We just completed our internal review and are planning to change the supplier tier for Redwood from ‘Standard’ to ‘Platform’ for the upcoming Order Form (ACME-4521). Before we finalize, procurement and legal need some clarifications about vendor flow-downs:

- Which third-party subprocessors (if any) will process customer content under this Order Form change?
- Do you have a current subprocessor matrix and dates of engagement (SaaS connectors, monitoring, telemetry vendors)?
- Our legal team also asked whether Redwood's current DPA covers the new data handling expectations tied to the Platform tier; if not, what redlines do you expect on the Order Form / MSA?

Could you share the subprocessor list and confirm whether the attached procurement questionnaire is sufficient for your legal team to complete? We would like to avoid a full MSA rework if an Order Form addendum + vendor flow-down notice suffices.

Thanks — can we aim to have docs by Wednesday this week?

Best,

On Tue, Mar 22, 2027 at 08:37 AM jasmine_liu@redwood.com wrote:
> Thanks Sofia — looping in our legal and SE leads to pull the materials together.

I reviewed the draft redlines (redlines_orderform_v2.docx) and the procurement questionnaire. Summary of legal items:

1) Subprocessor notification: acceptable as a notice + thirty-day right to object for specific processors that introduce new processing categories. We will provide a named subprocessor list and a catch-all clause for future additions with prior notice.
2) DPA compatibility: Redwood's DPA currently covers the processing purposes and security controls requested but we recommend: (a) a short Recital in the Order Form referencing the DPA version; (b) a confirmation clause that the DPA governs personal data, and (c) if Acme requires stricter retention or deletion controls for Platform tier, we will need to capture that in an Order Form Schedule (not change the master DPA).
3) Flow-downs: we can accept a reasonable set of flow-down obligations to subprocessors (security controls, breach notification). We will not accept unlimited liability flow-downs — recommend a carve for indirect damages in subprocessor terms.

I've tracked suggested edits in the attached docx. If Procurement wants more detail on specific subprocessors (e.g., monitoring provider), Dev can confirm the data they access.

-Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Laura, Jasmine — quick technical clarifications to support the legal notes:

- Monitoring/telemetry vendor (OpsSight) — reads anonymized telemetry (no customer prompt content), stores aggregated metrics for 90 days.
- Log retention (InfraLog) — stores request/response metadata, encrypted at rest, 30 day retention by default; retention can be reduced via customer order form one-off.
- Auth provider (Authly) — processes user identity tokens (no application content).

I'll attach a short subprocessor matrix export with the categories and contact dates. If Acme needs SOC2 report or a security questionnaire, point me to the specific section and I'll pull the artifact.
